title: Host Cancellations and the Reliability Holdback on Payout Methods Re-Sends
content:
A host's recent cancellations of bookings bear on how much of a returned balance is re-sent to their Payout Methods ahead of the next scheduled run. The re-send reliability holdback counts the host cancellations initiated by the host and recorded on the host account less than 12 whole months before the re-send: 6 percent for 2 or more, 3 percent for one, and nothing for none. The holdback is a percentage of the held balance, kept for the next scheduled run.

## What is counted

- **Records:** the host cancellation records on the host's Host Accounts record whose initiator is the host. Cancellations recorded as initiated by Roamhaven are not counted.
- **Window:** cancellations recorded less than 12 whole months before the re-send. A cancellation recorded exactly 12 whole months before the re-send is outside the window.

## Holdback by count

| Host-initiated cancellations recorded in the window | Reliability holdback, percent of the held balance |
|---|---|
| 2 or more | 6 percent |
| 1 | 3 percent |
| None | Nothing |

## Hypothetical cases (re-send dated 2026-08-20)

| Cancellations on the host account | Counted | Holdback |
|---|---|---|
| One initiated by the host on 2026-02-11 | 1 | 3 percent |
| One initiated by the host on 2026-02-11 and one initiated by Roamhaven on 2026-05-30 | 1 | 3 percent |
| Two initiated by the host, on 2025-08-21 and 2026-06-01 | 2 | 6 percent |
| One initiated by the host on 2025-08-20 (exactly 12 whole months earlier) | 0 | Nothing |

**Hypothetical amount.** On an imagined held balance of USD 3090.00 with 2 host-initiated cancellations in the window, the reliability holdback is 6 percent, USD 185.40.
